quests.hint: Changing jobs frequently instead of staying in one role for long.
quests.explanation: It compares switching jobs often to hopping quickly from one spot to the next.
quests.meaning: The practice of changing jobs frequently.
quests.sampleUsage: Job-hopping used to look bad on a resume, but attitudes have changed a lot.

quests.hint: Thinking about situations from an international, worldwide perspective.
quests.explanation: An 'outlook' is a way of viewing things, here widened to include the whole world.
quests.meaning: A perspective that considers international or worldwide factors.
quests.sampleUsage: The new CEO brought a global outlook that helped the company expand overseas.

quests.hint: A system for making and delivering goods that breaks down easily.
quests.explanation: 'Fragile' items break under small amounts of pressure, just like an unstable delivery system.
quests.meaning: A system of production and delivery that is easily disrupted.
quests.sampleUsage: The factory closure exposed just how fragile their supply chain really was.

quests.hint: Buying something suddenly, without planning to beforehand.
quests.explanation: An 'impulse' is a sudden urge, describing a purchase made on instinct rather than thought.
quests.meaning: Buying something suddenly, without planning it in advance.
quests.sampleUsage: She's trying to cut back on impulse buying by making a shopping list first.

quests.hint: Giving someone gentle guidance without forcing a decision.
quests.explanation: A physical nudge is a light push, matching the gentle, non-forceful style of the advice.
quests.meaning: To give someone gentle guidance, without forcing a decision.
quests.sampleUsage: The teacher just nudged him in the right direction instead of giving the answer.
quests.correctAnswer: Nudge someone in the right direction
quests.expression: Nudge someone in the right direction
quests.textToSpeak: Nudge someone in the right direction

quests.hint: Trying to do so many things that none of them get proper attention.
quests.explanation: Butter spread too thin over bread barely covers it, just like divided energy across too much.
quests.meaning: To take on too many tasks, leaving too little time or energy for each.
quests.sampleUsage: Between three jobs and volunteering, she's spreading herself too thin.

quests.hint: Having very little time left to finish something important.
quests.explanation: Pressure suggests a weight pressing down, here caused by a shrinking deadline.
quests.meaning: Having very little time to complete something.
quests.sampleUsage: Working under time pressure, the team still delivered the report on schedule.

quests.hint: Choosing to wait for a bigger reward instead of an immediate one.
quests.explanation: 'Gratification' is the pleasure of a reward, which this phrase deliberately postpones.
quests.meaning: To resist an immediate reward in order to gain a bigger one later.
quests.sampleUsage: Saving for a house means learning to delay gratification on smaller purchases.

quests.hint: Spending time or money on your own growth and future.
quests.explanation: Just like financial investing, the effort now is expected to pay off later.
quests.meaning: Time or money spent on your own personal growth or future.
quests.sampleUsage: Taking that coding course was really an investment in herself.

quests.hint: The group of work contacts that can support your career.
quests.explanation: A 'network' pictures connected points, here people linked together through work.
quests.meaning: A group of professional contacts that can support your career.
quests.sampleUsage: He built his professional network by attending industry conferences every year.

quests.hint: Becoming more visible or well known in your field.
quests.explanation: A raised profile stands out clearly, unlike one that stays low and unnoticed.
quests.meaning: To become more visible or well known, especially professionally.
quests.sampleUsage: Speaking at conferences really helped raise her profile in the industry.

quests.hint: Gaining someone's genuine admiration through your actions.
quests.explanation: Respect here is treated like something worked for, not simply given for free.
quests.meaning: To gain someone's genuine admiration through your actions.
quests.sampleUsage: He earned his team's respect by admitting his mistake immediately.

quests.hint: Planning carefully by considering what will happen after your next action.
quests.explanation: It comes from chess, where skilled players plan multiple moves before acting.
quests.meaning: To plan carefully by anticipating future consequences.
quests.sampleUsage: Good negotiators think several moves ahead before making an offer.

quests.hint: Protecting yourself from loss by keeping more than one option open.
quests.explanation: A hedge is a barrier that limits risk, borrowed here from betting and investing.
quests.meaning: To protect yourself from loss by keeping more than one option open.
quests.sampleUsage: She applied to several graduate programs to hedge her bets.

quests.hint: Having a backup plan ready in case things don't go as expected.
quests.explanation: 'Contingency' means something that might happen, so the plan prepares for that possibility.
quests.meaning: To have a backup plan ready in case the original one fails.
quests.sampleUsage: Always have a contingency plan when travelling during storm season.

quests.hint: Caring more about what actually gets achieved than how the effort looks.
quests.explanation: Being 'driven' by results means outcomes, not just effort, guide every decision.
quests.meaning: An attitude focused mainly on achieving clear, measurable outcomes.
quests.sampleUsage: Their new manager has a results-driven mindset that pushed the team to hit every target.

quests.hint: A saying about how consistency beats rushing in the long run.
quests.explanation: It comes from the fable of the tortoise, whose slow, steady pace beats the fast hare.
quests.meaning: Consistent, careful effort leads to success more reliably than rushing.
quests.sampleUsage: He never studies all night before exams; slow and steady wins the race for him.
quests.correctAnswer: Slow and steady wins the race
quests.expression: Slow and steady wins the race
quests.textToSpeak: Slow and steady wins the race

quests.hint: Trying something new that feels a little uncomfortable at first.
quests.explanation: A 'comfort zone' pictures a safe, familiar space, so stepping out means facing the unfamiliar.
quests.meaning: To try something new or unfamiliar that feels uncomfortable at first.
quests.sampleUsage: Signing up for the public speaking class meant stepping outside her comfort zone.

quests.hint: What you'd say about a decision now, if you could look back on it later.
quests.explanation: 'Hindsight' literally means sight looking backward, seeing clearly only after the fact.
quests.meaning: Looking back at a past event with the understanding you have now.
quests.sampleUsage: In hindsight, we should have booked the tickets a month earlier.

quests.hint: Having a clear understanding of your own feelings and behaviour.
quests.explanation: It combines 'self' with 'aware,' describing honest awareness pointed inward.
quests.meaning: Having a clear understanding of your own character, feelings, and behaviour.
quests.sampleUsage: She's self-aware enough to know when she needs a break.

quests.hint: A sense about something that comes from instinct, not clear reasoning.
quests.explanation: Strong emotions and instincts are often felt physically in the stomach, or 'gut.'
quests.meaning: An instinctive sense about something, not based on clear reasoning.
quests.sampleUsage: I had a gut feeling that the deal wasn't going to go through.

quests.hint: Refusing to change your opinion, even when others disagree.
quests.explanation: A soldier who stays at their gun position under attack refuses to retreat or give up.
quests.meaning: To refuse to change your opinion or decision, despite pressure.
quests.sampleUsage: Everyone disagreed with her plan, but she stuck to her guns.

quests.hint: Seeing mistakes as useful information rather than pure disappointment.
quests.explanation: 'Feedback' describes information used to improve, reframing failure as genuinely useful.
quests.meaning: To see mistakes as useful information for improvement, not just as disappointment.
quests.sampleUsage: Good coaches teach athletes to treat failure as feedback, not as the end of the road.

quests.hint: Stepping back to see a situation more clearly and calmly.
quests.explanation: Perspective is a viewing angle, so gaining it means seeing the full picture more clearly.
quests.meaning: To step back and see a situation more clearly and calmly.
quests.sampleUsage: Talking to a friend helped him gain some perspective on the breakup.

quests.hint: Doubting a decision you already made.
quests.explanation: A 'second guess' comes after the first decision, questioning it after the fact.
quests.meaning: To doubt a decision you have already made.
quests.sampleUsage: Stop second-guessing yourself; you prepared well for this interview.

quests.hint: Developing the ability to recover well from difficulties.
quests.explanation: Resilient materials bend under pressure and spring back, just like a strong, adaptable mindset.
quests.meaning: To develop the ability to recover well from difficulties.
quests.sampleUsage: Facing setbacks early in her career helped her build resilience.

quests.hint: A difficult talk about something uncomfortable or emotional.
quests.explanation: 'Hard' here describes emotional difficulty, not physical toughness.
quests.meaning: A difficult conversation about something uncomfortable or emotional.
quests.sampleUsage: He finally had the hard conversation about ending their business partnership.

quests.hint: Listening to someone without criticising or forming a negative opinion.
quests.explanation: It promises an open, accepting response instead of silent criticism.
quests.meaning: Without criticising or forming a negative opinion of someone.
quests.sampleUsage: A good therapist listens without judgement.

quests.hint: A sudden point when everything suddenly makes sense.
quests.explanation: Clarity means clearness, so this pictures confusion suddenly lifting like fog.
quests.meaning: A sudden point when a situation becomes completely clear.
quests.sampleUsage: She had a moment of clarity and realised exactly what she wanted to do next.

quests.hint: Noticing small hints or signals that others might miss.
quests.explanation: A 'cue' is a small signal, and 'picking up on' it means catching something easy to overlook.
quests.meaning: To notice small signals or hints that others might miss.
quests.sampleUsage: A good waiter picks up on subtle cues, like an empty glass, without being asked.
